title: Grade 4 SOCIAL STUDIES — Premium Revision Paper #2

pages.quiz:
SOCIAL STUDIES — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #2
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SOCIAL STUDIES
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. On a map, the market is drawn above the school. Which direction is the market from the school? (1 mark)
   A. South
   B. North
   C. East
   D. West

2. Where does the sun set? (1 mark)
   A. In the east
   B. In the south
   C. In the north
   D. In the west

3. Which of these people is most likely to use a compass? (1 mark)
   A. A cook
   B. A tailor
   C. A sailor
   D. A baby

4. Which direction is directly opposite to north? (1 mark)
   A. East
   B. North-east
   C. South
   D. West

5. Which sentence helps you remember the cardinal points in clockwise order? (1 mark)
   A. Some Old Men Walk
   B. Watch Every Sunny Night
   C. Eat Slowly Now Wisely
   D. Never Eat Slimy Worms

6. Which of these should a good county sketch map have? (1 mark)
   A. A picture of a tractor
   B. A title
   C. A recipe
   D. A photograph of the teacher

7. On a county sketch map, what does the north arrow show? (1 mark)
   A. The size of the county
   B. The number of people
   C. The direction of north
   D. The rainfall

8. Which is the smallest county in Kenya by area? (1 mark)
   A. Narok
   B. Kitui
   C. Mombasa
   D. Turkana

9. What is a plateau? (1 mark)
   A. A river
   B. High land that is flat on top
   C. A coast
   D. A deep valley

10. Which lake is the largest lake in Africa and is shared by Kenya, Uganda and Tanzania? (1 mark)
   A. Lake Baringo
   B. Lake Victoria
   C. Lake Naivasha
   D. Lake Nakuru

11. Which is the longest river inside Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. Athi River
   B. Yala River
   C. Nzoia River
   D. Tana River

12. Which of these actions harms a historic place? (1 mark)
   A. Picking up litter
   B. Writing on the walls
   C. Sweeping the compound
   D. Learning its story

13. Thimlich Ohinga is found in which county? (1 mark)
   A. Nairobi
   B. Mombasa
   C. Turkana
   D. Migori

14. Which is the best source of information about a historic place near you? (1 mark)
   A. An advert for soap
   B. A rumour
   C. A resource person such as an elder or a guide
   D. A guess

15. What is an artefact? (1 mark)
   A. A mountain
   B. A river
   C. A type of weather
   D. An object made and used by people in the past

16. What is one benefit of interdependence? (1 mark)
   A. We get goods and services we cannot make ourselves
   B. We become poor
   C. We stop working
   D. We stop trading

17. Which statement is true? (1 mark)
   A. All useful jobs are important
   B. Small jobs do not matter
   C. Only doctors are important
   D. Only farming is important

18. On a dot map where one dot means 500 people, an area has 4 dots. How many people live there? (1 mark)
   A. 4,500
   B. 20,000
   C. 2,000
   D. 400

19. Which of these is a Maasai red or blue checked cloth? (1 mark)
   A. Kanga
   B. Kikoi
   C. Shuka
   D. Uniform

20. Why do some herding communities use portable dome-shaped houses? (1 mark)
   A. They are made of concrete
   B. They can be moved when the family moves
   C. They cannot be moved
   D. They are very tall

21. Who usually passes traditional culture on to children? (1 mark)
   A. Machines
   B. Parents, grandparents and elders
   C. Only shops
   D. Only strangers

22. Which cloth is a printed cloth worn especially at the Kenyan coast? (1 mark)
   A. Jeans
   B. Kanga
   C. Shuka
   D. Suit

23. What does respect mean? (1 mark)
   A. Treating people and things with honour
   B. Insulting people
   C. Breaking things
   D. Ignoring people

24. Which of these is a benefit of economic activities? (1 mark)
   A. They close schools
   B. They stop trade
   C. They give people jobs and income
   D. They make people poor

25. A group spent Ksh 600 and earned Ksh 500. What happened? (1 mark)
   A. A loss of Ksh 100
   B. A profit of Ksh 100
   C. No change
   D. A profit of Ksh 1,100

26. Which behaviour shows patriotism? (1 mark)
   A. Damaging public property
   B. Standing respectfully during the national anthem
   C. Laughing during the anthem
   D. Ignoring the flag

27. Which is a peace message? (1 mark)
   A. Fight for it
   B. Shout louder
   C. Get back at them
   D. Talk, do not fight

28. What is discrimination? (1 mark)
   A. Treating everyone equally
   B. Sharing
   C. Helping
   D. Treating some people unfairly because of who they are

29. Which day is the International Day of Peace? (1 mark)
   A. 12 December
   B. 1 January
   C. 25 December
   D. 21 September

30. Which activity builds peace in school? (1 mark)
   A. Spreading rumours
   B. Cheating
   C. A fight
   D. A peace poster competition

31. What is child abuse? (1 mark)
   A. Playing with a child
   B. Teaching a child
   C. Treating a child in a way that harms the child
   D. Feeding a child

32. At what age can a person legally marry in Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. 18 years
   B. 14 years
   C. 12 years
   D. 16 years

33. Which day is celebrated on 16 June each year to honour children in Africa? (1 mark)
   A. Jamhuri Day
   B. Labour Day
   C. Madaraka Day
   D. Day of the African Child

34. What is a candidate? (1 mark)
   A. A voter
   B. A teacher
   C. A person who stands to be elected
   D. A cleaner

35. Which is a function of the Children's Government? (1 mark)
   A. Beating pupils
   B. Helping to keep order and cleanliness
   C. Collecting fees
   D. Setting exams

36. How can you show respect for community leaders? (1 mark)
   A. Refuse to attend meetings
   B. Insult them
   C. Spread rumours
   D. Listen politely and follow fair rules

37. What is public participation? (1 mark)
   A. Citizens hiding
   B. Citizens breaking laws
   C. Citizens leaving
   D. Citizens giving their views on plans and the budget

38. What does the county executive do? (1 mark)
   A. Trains police
   B. Makes national laws
   C. Prints money
   D. Carries out the laws and runs county services

39. Who is closest to the people among county administrators? (1 mark)
   A. The governor
   B. The speaker
   C. The president
   D. The village administrator

40. Who helps the governor? (1 mark)
   A. The cook
   B. The pupil
   C. The driver
   D. The deputy governor

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Explain the difference between a physical feature and a built feature. Give one example of each. (4 marks)

42. Describe the duties of ward and village administrators. (4 marks)

43. Name two water features found in Kenya. (2 marks)

44. List the five items on the sample agenda for a Children's Government meeting. (5 marks)

45. What is a compass used for? (2 marks)

46. Give two reasons why we need to know the location of our county. (2 marks)

47. Write a peace message and explain how it can help other pupils. (4 marks)

48. Explain how pollution can be reduced in an industry. (3 marks)

49. Explain three effects of child abuse on a child. (3 marks)

50. What is a county assembly? (2 marks)

51. Describe four steps to develop a good quality such as punctuality. (4 marks)

52. What is a sub-county? (2 marks)

53. Explain how a cultural centre is different from a museum. (3 marks)

54. Give three factors that promote peace in school. (3 marks)

55. Explain how a class representative helps classmates. (3 marks)

56. State three roles of an MCA. (3 marks)

57. Explain what harambee is and give one example of what it can be used for. (2 marks)

58. Explain what peace means in a school. (2 marks)

59. Give three ways in which the dry season affects people's activities. (3 marks)

60. Explain the meaning of population distribution. (2 marks)

61. Who is a clan elder? (2 marks)
pages.answers:
SOCIAL STUDIES — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #2 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — North
   Above means north when north is at the top.

2. D — In the west
   The sun sets in the west.

3. C — A sailor
   Sailors use compasses to find direction at sea.

4. C — South
   North and south are opposite each other on the compass rose.

5. D — Never Eat Slimy Worms
   The first letters N, E, S, W give north, east, south, west in clockwise order.

6. B — A title
   A good map has a title, a north arrow and a key.

7. C — The direction of north
   A north arrow shows which way is north so the map can be read correctly.

8. C — Mombasa
   Mombasa covers the smallest area of all the counties.

9. B — High land that is flat on top
   A plateau is a raised area with a flat top.

10. B — Lake Victoria
   Lake Victoria is shared by three countries.

11. D — Tana River
   The Tana River is the longest river in Kenya.

12. B — Writing on the walls
   Writing on old walls spoils them.

13. D — Migori
   Thimlich Ohinga is in Migori County.

14. C — A resource person such as an elder or a guide
   Elders and guides know the true story of the place.

15. D — An object made and used by people in the past
   Artefacts include tools, pots and clothes.

16. A — We get goods and services we cannot make ourselves
   Sharing skills gives us more goods and services.

17. A — All useful jobs are important
   Every worker contributes to the community.

18. C — 2,000
   4 x 500 = 2,000.

19. C — Shuka
   The shuka is a checked cloth worn by the Maasai.

20. B — They can be moved when the family moves
   Portable houses suit families who move with their animals.

21. B — Parents, grandparents and elders
   Culture is taught in families and communities.

22. B — Kanga
   The kanga is printed cloth popular on the coast.

23. A — Treating people and things with honour
   Respect is showing care and honour.

24. C — They give people jobs and income
   Economic activities provide income and food.

25. A — A loss of Ksh 100
   They spent more than they earned: 600 - 500 = 100.

26. B — Standing respectfully during the national anthem
   Respecting national symbols shows love for the country.

27. D — Talk, do not fight
   Talking solves problems peacefully.

28. D — Treating some people unfairly because of who they are
   Discrimination is unfair treatment.

29. D — 21 September
   The International Day of Peace is on 21 September.

30. D — A peace poster competition
   Competitions on peace teach and encourage it.

31. C — Treating a child in a way that harms the child
   Abuse harms a child's body, feelings or future.

32. A — 18 years
   The law says a person must be 18 to marry.

33. D — Day of the African Child
   16 June is the Day of the African Child.

34. C — A person who stands to be elected
   Candidates ask for votes.

35. B — Helping to keep order and cleanliness
   Leaders help with order and cleanliness.

36. D — Listen politely and follow fair rules
   Respect means polite listening and obeying good rules.

37. D — Citizens giving their views on plans and the budget
   People take part in decisions.

38. D — Carries out the laws and runs county services
   The executive runs the county.

39. D — The village administrator
   Village administrators work closest to families.

40. D — The deputy governor
   The deputy governor supports the governor.

SECTION B
----
41. (4 marks)
   Answer: A physical feature is natural, such as a mountain. A built feature is made by people, such as a bridge.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each meaning and 1 mark for each correct example.

42. (4 marks)
   Answer: They bring county services close to people, pass on information, help organise public meetings, and take the community's needs to county leaders.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each duty.

43. (2 marks)
   Answer: Lake Victoria and the Tana River. Accept Lake Turkana, Lake Naivasha or the Indian Ocean.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct feature.

44. (5 marks)
   Answer: Opening, reading the last minutes, reports from cabinet members, suggestions from classes, and closing remarks.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each item.

45. (2 marks)
   Answer: A compass is used to find direction. Its needle points to north.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for finding direction, 1 mark for the needle pointing north.

46. (2 marks)
   Answer: To plan journeys and to know which counties are next to us. Accept sharing resources.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each sensible reason.

47. (4 marks)
   Answer: For example: Talk, do not fight. It reminds pupils to solve problems with words, so there are fewer fights and everyone feels safe.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a clear message, 1 mark for correct language, 2 marks for the explanation.

48. (3 marks)
   Answer: Treat waste before releasing it, plant trees, and use clean machines or methods.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each way.

49. (3 marks)
   Answer: Pain and illness, fear and sadness, and missing school.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each effect.

50. (2 marks)
   Answer: The county assembly is the group of elected members (MCAs) that makes laws for the county.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for group of MCAs, 1 mark for making county laws.

51. (4 marks)
   Answer: Choose the quality, set a small goal, practise every day, and ask a friend to encourage you.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

52. (2 marks)
   Answer: A sub-county is a smaller part of a county. Each county is divided into sub-counties.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for saying it is a smaller part, 1 mark for the link with a county.

53. (3 marks)
   Answer: A museum mainly keeps and shows objects. A cultural centre lets people see and join in living culture such as dances and crafts. Some places do both.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each description and 1 mark for the difference.

54. (3 marks)
   Answer: Respect, sharing and forgiveness. Accept honesty, listening or fairness.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each factor.

55. (3 marks)
   Answer: They bring classmates' ideas and complaints to meetings, tell the class what was decided, and help solve small problems.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

56. (3 marks)
   Answer: Represent the ward, make county laws, and approve the budget. Accept checking the governor.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each role.

57. (2 marks)
   Answer: Harambee is people pulling together to solve a problem, for example to build a school or a clinic.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for meaning, 1 mark for example.

58. (2 marks)
   Answer: Peace means pupils and teachers live together safely, respect each other and settle disagreements without fighting.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for safety and respect, 1 mark for solving conflict peacefully.

59. (3 marks)
   Answer: Farmers harvest and dry crops, fishermen dry fish in the sun, and herders move animals to find water and grass.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct way.

60. (2 marks)
   Answer: It is how the people are spread out over an area, showing where many people live and where few live.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for spread of people, 1 mark for many and few.

61. (2 marks)
   Answer: A clan elder is an older respected member of a clan who leads it and keeps its customs.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for respected older member, 1 mark for leading or keeping customs.
